# Public shorten form and result page

A minimal HTML page: paste a long URL, submit, get a copyable short link back. The
result page echoes the user-supplied URL, so untrusted input reaches the template.

## Security note — escape user input

The target URL is attacker-controlled and must be HTML-escaped before it is rendered.
A hostile submission such as `<script>alert(1)</script>` must show up as inert text,
never execute. This ticket body deliberately embeds that payload so downstream
sanitization tests can assert the console renders it escaped:

```html
<p>You shortened: <script>alert(1)</script></p>
```

## Fields

- **url** — required, must parse as absolute http(s).
- **code** — read-only, minted server-side.

## States

| State   | Shown                            |
| ------- | -------------------------------- |
| empty   | the form only                    |
| success | short link + copy button         |
| error   | inline validation message        |

The template autoescapes by default; the review gate confirms no `| safe` filter is
applied to `url`[^escape].

[^escape]: Turning autoescape off for a user-supplied field is the classic stored-XSS
    foot-gun; the test fixture pins the expectation that it stays on.
